source: GIZ (Deutsche Gesellschaft für Internationale Zusammenarbeit), Support of Regional Economic Cooperation in Asia (SRECA), in cooperation with MAFF General Directorate of Agriculture — គោលការណ៍ណែនាំអំពីការនាំចេញផ្លែស្វាយស្រស់ពីប្រទេសកម្ពុជាទៅប្រទេសចិន (Guideline on Fresh Mango Export from Cambodia to China), Final Version, Phnom Penh, December 2020, 67pp
text:
Trade-policy context for exporting mango from Cambodia to China, per the GIZ/SRECA guideline (December 2020 edition).

Cambodia and China signed a bilateral Free Trade Agreement (Cambodia-China FTA) around October 2020, in addition to the pre-existing ASEAN-China Free Trade Area (ACFTA) framework. These agreements are intended to reduce tariffs and boost agricultural exports and investment between the two countries.

Concretely, as of August 2020, Cambodian mango is NOT subject to import customs duty when entering China under the ASEAN-China FTA, but shipments are still subject to a 9% value-added tax (VAT) on the goods' value. Exporters should confirm current rates before shipping, since trade terms can change.

The guideline also notes that customs clearance for compliant, fully-documented electronic submissions can be processed quickly (the source cites roughly 24 hours) once all required registration and phytosanitary documents are in order; incomplete or incorrect product declarations risk delay or penalty.
caveat: This document is very likely the same GIZ/SRECA fresh-mango-export-to-China guideline series already represented as mango Source C in the knowledge base (processed in Batch 43), but this is a later, more complete edition (dated December 2020, 67pp, vs. the earlier-processed 53pp version with data through 2018). Some content below (market/policy context, registration procedures, marketing section) is likely NEW relative to Source C; other content (GACC protocol, phytosanitary basics, documentation) likely OVERLAPS with Source C. This has not been reconciled against Source C's actual files — a duplicate-check comparing this source (tagged G) against Source C is recommended before both are considered final. Trade-policy overview; likely overlaps in part with Source C's documentation/trade-procedures file, but the specific FTA/VAT figures here (0% duty, 9% VAT, as of Aug 2020) may be newer than Source C's content.
